skills.name: Stand-down destination setup
skills.description: Use this when a changelog stand-down bot (or share-template copy) has no destination configured yet, or the user wants to change where digests post.
skills.content:
---
name: Stand-down destination setup
description: >-
  Use this when a changelog stand-down bot (or share-template copy) has no
  destination configured yet, or the user wants to change where digests post.
---
Use when no primary destination is saved yet, or the user asks to change destinations.

## Steps

1. Ask where digests should post. Offer: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, GitHub Discussions. Multi-select is fine when several apply. Use a question widget with multiSelect when available.

2. For each chosen destination, check whether that connector is already connected. If it is not, start the normal connector connect/auth card for that service. Never ask the user to paste tokens or secrets. Mobile OAuth is fine.

3. After auth succeeds, confirm the concrete target:
   - Slack: channel (and workspace if ambiguous)
   - Microsoft Teams: team and channel
   - Discord: server and channel
   - GitHub Discussions: owner/repo and Discussion category (or a recurring thread if they name one)

4. Save the chosen destinations and concrete targets to agent memory (profile tier for standing config). Mark unchosen adapters as stubs.

5. On Monday runs, post only to live destinations. If a chosen adapter fails or is not connected at run time, deliver the digest in chat with the error and which stubs remain.

## Do not

- Re-ask when a destination is already configured unless the user wants to change it.
- Post to stub adapters.
- Invent channel/repo names; confirm with the user.

routines.name: Weekly changelog stand-down
routines.description: Every Monday morning, summarize prior-week merged PRs and releases for watched repos and post via configured destinations.
routines.content:
Weekly changelog stand-down for watched GitHub repos.

1) Load from agent memory: watched repo list and configured destination adapters (Slack / Teams / Discord / GitHub Discussions). If no watched repos are saved, stay quiet and note in chat that repos still need configuring — do not invent repos.

2) For each watched repo, pull merged PRs and releases from the prior calendar week (Monday–Sunday in the user's local timezone). Prefer GitHub connector or gh. Fact-first only; never invent metrics.

3) If zero merges and zero releases across all watched repos: stay quiet (no chat message, no external post).

4) Otherwise draft a short skim-friendly digest: friendly, direct, technical. No AI-isms, no em dashes. State facts first. Group by repo when watching more than one.

5) Post only through live configured destination adapters. Never post to stub/unconfigured adapters. Never post externally until destinations are configured. Do not invent channel/repo/Discussion targets.

6) On any adapter failure: deliver the full digest in chat with the error and which adapters failed/remain stubs.

7) Dry run = digest only in chat unless the user explicitly asked to post.

Fires on:
- cron `0 9 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
